newsitem.title: UK: Caymans to create monetary authority in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Caymans to create monetary authority in 1997.

text.p: The Cayman Islands said on Monday it was setting up a monetary authority next year to manage its currency and regulate its financial industry.

The authority will be formed from the integration of the islands' currency board and its Financial Services Supervision Department (FSSD) in January 1997, after the government passed the necessary legislation on Friday, the islands said in a statement released in London.

"The development of the monetary authority is a result of our continued commitment to review and enhance the strength of our regulatory regime to ensure that the confidence placed in the Cayman Islands by the international community is fostered," said George McCarthy, the Cayman Islands' financial secretary.
The Bank of England has been advising the Caribbean island group on setting up the body, which is expected to comprise 40 staff members by the end of the first year.
The islands' FSSD is responsible for regulating 573 banks, 407 captive insurance companies, 32 licensed company managers and 1,241 mutual funds.
Similar monetary authorities have been set up in Hong Kong, Singapore, Bahrain and Bermuda. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
